de.my_domain.abalone.gui

Class BoardPanel

  • java.lang.Object
    • java.awt.Component
      • java.awt.Container
        • javax.swing.JComponent
          • javax.swing.JPanel
            • de.my_domain.abalone.gui.BoardPanel
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    java.awt.image.ImageObserver, java.awt.MenuContainer, java.io.Serializable, javax.accessibility.Accessible

    public class BoardPanel
extends javax.swing.JPanel
    The BoardPanel Class. The BoardPanel class is a JPanel. It is used to represent the current state of a Board game. It hold many GridPanel, as well as BallPanel objects to do so. In the lower left and right corner it holds the current ball count of each player. The BoardPanel also offers methods to either completely reconstruct the contents of the panel according to a Board object - this is usually done when more or less BallPanel objects are needed - or to mutate the current BallPanel object. It also implements the action handling of the ball panels within the BoardPanel. So it is able to select or highlight a ball panel. It also provides the user a way to undo the selection completely.

        public BoardPanel(GameFrame frame)
        The BoardPanel constructor creates a new BoardPanel object, which holds the current representation of an Abalone Board game. It initialized the BoardPanel, sets the background color and adds BallPanels on itself, each of which represent a slot in the game.

      • setInformation

        void setInformation(Board model)
        The setInformation method updates the color information of each ball by asking the Board object model which color each of the slots has. It also sets the information displayed in the CountPanel object.
        Parameters:
        model - Is the model object from which the method knows the color of each ball, as well as the count information.

      • customizeLayout

        private void customizeLayout(Board model)
        The customizeLayout method first removes all the existing objects from the BoardPanel, then sets the Layout to a GridBagLayout. Each of the BallPanel objects created by the initializeBoard method are then added to the GridBagLayout. Additionally a GridPanel is assigned to empty room amongst the BallPanel objects. The GridPanel exists to design the room in between to BallPanel objects. Finally, a method is called to add the CountPanel objects.
        Parameters:
        model - Is the model object from which the method knows which cell in the array is a BallPanel.

      • customizeCountPanelLayout

        private void customizeCountPanelLayout()
        The customizeCountPanelLayout method adds the human as well as the machine CountPanel to the BoardPanel. The panels are added in the right respectively left lower corner of the Panel. The width and height of the Panels are twofold of the width respectively height of the BallPanels.

      • ballClicked

        private void ballClicked(BallPanel clicked)
        The ballClicked method is called when a ball is clicked. As a parameter is gets the clicked BallPanel. The method first checks if the machine is busy and if appropriated locks the input and informs the user about the lock. Else it checks if a ball has been clicked before. If not it selects given ball, else if makes a move to the clicked ball. If a selected ball is clicked again it is unselected.
        Parameters:
        clicked - Is the BallPanel that has been clicked.

      • move

        private void move(BallPanel ball)
        The move method first gets the coordinates of the upcoming move and then deselects the selected ball. It also removes highlighting of all the possible moves.
        Parameters:
        ball - Is the BallPanel that has been clicked last.

        Parameters:

        Parameters:
        firstSelected - Is the BallPanel which has been selected.
